questions.prompt: What does the 'infer' keyword do in a TypeScript conditional type?

options.text: It casts any variable to the 'any' type.
It introduces a type variable within the extends clause to be deduced from the matched type.
It imports an external module asynchronously.

questions.explanation: 'infer' allows you to declare a type variable inside the condition to capture and extract an internal type dynamically.

questions.prompt: Why is a Branded Type useful in TypeScript?

options.text: It compresses the output bundle size.
It attaches a phantom compile-time tag to a primitive type (like string), preventing accidental assignment between different semantic identifiers like UserId and OrderId.
It makes the property accessible only in React components.

questions.explanation: Branded types enforce nominal typing, stopping bugs where strings of different semantic meanings are accidentally passed in the wrong parameter order.

questions.prompt: What does the tsconfig.json compiler option 'noUncheckedIndexedAccess' accomplish?

options.text: It adds 'undefined' to the return type of array and object index lookups, forcing developers to check if an element exists before using it.
It converts all arrays into tuples.
It compiles arrays to WebAssembly memory buffers.

questions.explanation: By default, arr[0] assumes the element is defined. 'noUncheckedIndexedAccess' types it as T | undefined, preventing out-of-bounds runtime crashes.
